newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ONIC urges EU to export more wheat soon.
newsitem.headline: French ONIC urges EU to export more wheat soon.

text.p: The European Union should export more wheat soon to avoid a potential dip in prices when southern hemisphere crops arrive, France's ONIC cereals office said on Wednesday.
While welcoming recent awards of EU export licences, ONIC said now was the time to sell more from Europe's bumper crop.

"The level of certificates delivered so far is enough not to make everyone scream, but it is still reatively modest compared to three years ago," ONIC director general Alain Moulinier told a news conference.
"We would like to be as active as possible and we hope we can be so in the early part of the season when the opportunity is there," he said.

Moulinier was briefing reporters on ONIC's just-published estimates which suggest French wheat exports outside the EU could swell to 6.8 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July/June) from 3.75 million tonnes the year before.
ONIC put this year's French soft wheat harvest at a record 34.347 million tonnes, up from 29.825 million in 1995.
Figures provided by ONIC show that at almost three million tonnes, soft wheat and wheat flour exports allowed by the EU so far this season are under half the comparable level in 1994/95.

"If the Commission wants to return to the world market, it has every incentive to award certificates now, because world prices could fall further under the impact of promising Argentine and Australian crops," ONIC said in a report released alongside the monthly supply estimates.
The EU Commission has said it will export more wheat but is not prepared to undercut U.S. wheat prices. Although lower recently, these have been supported by tight U.S. wheat stocks.

Moulinier said some grain exporters represented at an ONIC meeting earlier on Wednesday complained that the Commission seemed to be using an average of soft red winter and hard red winter wheat prices when assessing its own exports.
But this benchmark was currently less representative than the cheaper soft white U.S. export wheat, Moulinier quoted the exporters as saying.
He backed the Commission in not wanting to compete with far cheaper levels quoted recently for new-crop Argentine wheat, saying these did "not make the world price". --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
